## [terraform-provider-talos 0.13.0-alpha.3](https://github.com/siderolabs/terraform-provider-talos/releases/tag/v0.13.0-alpha.3) (2026-11-25) Welcome to the v0.13.0-alpha.3 release of terraform-provider-talos! *This is a pre-release of terraform-provider-talos* Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/siderolabs/terraform-provider-talos/issues. ### New options `talos_machine_configuration` has a new `components` option to generate a configuration without Kubernetes, or without Kubernetes and etcd. `talos_cluster_health` has a new `k8s_endpoint` option to override the Kubernetes API endpoint used for the Kubernetes checks. `talos_cluster` has new optional `machine_secrets` and `machine_secrets_wo` arguments, and the `kubernetes_ca_certificate`, `talos_ca_certificate`, `etcd_ca_certificate` and `kubernetes_aggregator_ca_certificate` attributes: the CA certificates of the cluster, known at plan time. See the resource guide. ### talos_machine `talos_machine` can now be imported, and has a new `drain_timeout` attribute that caps how long pod eviction may take during an upgrade. `drain_on_upgrade` copes better with a create that runs before the cluster is ready: a node that has not joined the cluster yet is not drained, a node that is not Ready is drained but not waited for before it is uncordoned, and a node whose machine config sets `skipNodeRegistration` is never drained. A failed drain now uncordons the node again, and a node that does not come back Ready after an upgrade stays cordoned, with an error that says how to uncordon it. See the resource guide. When only the image tag changes, `talos_machine` first checks the running version and no longer upgrades or reboots a node that already runs it. This matters when the state is stale, for example with write-only credentials after a `talosctl upgrade`. ### Component Updates Talos sdk: v1.14.1 ### Contributors * Mickaël Canévet * Bart van der Schans * Fritz Schaal * RoFz ### Changes

# terraform-provider-talos

## Debugging

In a bash shell, build a debug version of this provider binary:

```bash
make build-debug
```

In Visual Studio Code, [start the provider in a debug session](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/debugging#starting-a-provider-in-debug-mode).

In a new bash shell, go into your terraform project directory, and run
terraform with `TF_REATTACH_PROVIDERS` set to the value printed in the VSCode debug windows.
